name: Cristo Rey Church

location.text: 1120 Canyon Road, Santa Fe, New Mexico

dates.note: Wikipedia: 'commissioned by Archbishop of Santa Fe Rudolph Gerken in 1939 and completed in 1940'; the Meem works list prints 'Cristo Rey Church, Santa Fe (1939)'. The exemplar year is 1940.

refs.title: Cristo Rey Church - Wikipedia
refs.note: 'claimed by some sources to be the largest adobe building in the United States'; 'requiring 150,000–200,000 individual adobes'; 'built from adobe, though it is supported by a hidden steel frame rather than relying completely on traditional building techniques'; 'The ceiling is supported on massive, corbeled vigas'. A title with the '(Santa Fe, New Mexico)' disambiguator answered 404.

refs.title: National Register of Historic Places Multiple Property Documentation, 'Buildings Designed by John Gaw Meem, 1925-1959' (NPGallery)
refs.note: 'In 1939, he received two church commissions in Santa Fe ... The latter stands as one of Meem's notable achievements.' The MPS cover document, not an individual nomination; whether the church is individually listed was not established.

note: Added 4 Sep 2026 as the largest thing the style ever built in real adobe -- and, on Wikipedia's account, on a hidden steel frame, which is the 'stucco over ... wood frame' half of the node's own vocabulary at church scale. No register number and no HABS record were found.
